questions.question: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.fact: Each water molecule is two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. Water is one of the few substances that expands when it freezes.

questions.question: Which gas do humans need to breathe in to live?
questions.fact: Air is only about 21% oxygen. At rest you breathe in and out roughly 12 to 20 times a minute.

questions.question: At what temperature in °C does water boil at sea level?
questions.fact: Water boils at lower temperatures up mountains: at the top of Everest it boils at only about 70 °C.

questions.question: What is the most common gas in Earth's air?
questions.fact: About 78% of the air is nitrogen and about 21% is oxygen. The rest is mostly argon.

questions.question: Which force keeps us on the ground?
questions.fact: You would weigh about six times less on the Moon, because its gravity is much weaker than Earth's.

questions.question: What do bees collect from flowers to make honey?
questions.fact: Bees visit flowers for nectar, which they turn into honey. Pollen sticks to them on the way, which is how they pollinate plants.

questions.question: What is the centre of an atom called?
questions.fact: An atom is mostly empty space. If the nucleus were the size of a marble, the whole atom would be bigger than a football stadium.

questions.question: Which part of a plant makes food from sunlight?
questions.fact: Leaves are green because of chlorophyll, which absorbs red and blue light and reflects green.

questions.question: What is the process plants use to make food from sunlight?
questions.fact: Photosynthesis uses sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make sugar, and gives off oxygen as a bonus.

questions.question: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.fact: Mercury was once used in thermometers, but it's toxic, so most modern thermometers use alcohol or electronics instead.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
questions.fact: Na comes from "natrium", the Latin name for sodium. Pure sodium is a soft metal that fizzes violently in water.

questions.question: At what temperature in °C does water freeze?
questions.fact: Salt water freezes at a lower temperature than fresh water, which is why salt is spread on icy roads.

questions.question: What do we call animals that eat only plants?
questions.fact: Some of the largest animals on land, like elephants and giraffes, are herbivores.

questions.question: Which colour of visible light has the longest wavelength?
questions.fact: Red light scatters least in the air, which is why sunsets look red and orange.

questions.question: How many colours are traditionally named in a rainbow?
questions.fact: The seven colours are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. Isaac Newton chose seven, partly to match the musical scale.

questions.question: What does a thermometer measure?
questions.fact: The first thermometers with a scale were made in the 1600s. The Celsius scale is named after Swedish astronomer Anders Celsius.

questions.question: Lightning is a giant spark of…
questions.fact: A lightning bolt can be about five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.

questions.question: What is a scientist who studies rocks called?
questions.fact: Geologists can tell the age of rocks from the layers they form in, a bit like reading the pages of a book.

questions.question: Sound travels fastest through which of these?
questions.fact: Sound travels about 15 times faster through steel than through air, and it can't travel through empty space at all.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for iron?
questions.fact: Fe comes from "ferrum", the Latin word for iron. Iron is what makes blood red.

questions.question: What are the balls of ice that fall during some storms called?
questions.fact: Hailstones grow by being tossed up and down inside storm clouds, adding a layer of ice each trip.

questions.question: Which vitamin are oranges famous for?
questions.fact: Sailors once got scurvy from a lack of vitamin C, which is why British sailors were given limes and nicknamed "limeys".

questions.question: What is the study of weather called?
questions.fact: The word "meteorology" comes from Greek "meteoron", meaning "thing high up in the sky".

questions.question: Which instrument records earthquakes?
questions.fact: Thousands of small earthquakes happen every day around the world, but most are too weak to feel.

questions.question: What is the pH of pure water?
questions.fact: A pH below 7 is acidic, like lemon juice, and above 7 is alkaline, like soap.

questions.question: What is the tallest type of tree in the world?
questions.fact: The tallest known tree, a coast redwood in California nicknamed "Hyperion", is over 115 metres tall.

questions.question: Which gas do plants give off during photosynthesis?
questions.fact: Ocean plants and algae make around half of the oxygen we breathe.

questions.question: What is the smallest unit of life?
questions.fact: Your body is made of tens of trillions of cells, and most of them are far too small to see without a microscope.

questions.question: What does DNA stand for?
questions.fact: If you uncoiled all the DNA in just one of your cells, it would be about two metres long.

questions.question: Roughly how fast does light travel?
questions.fact: Light from the Moon takes just over a second to reach us. Nothing in the universe travels faster than light.

questions.question: What is it called when a liquid turns into a gas?
questions.fact: Evaporation happens even without boiling: that's how puddles disappear on a sunny day.

questions.question: What is "dry ice"?
questions.fact: Dry ice is about −78 °C and turns straight from solid into gas, which makes the spooky "fog" effect at concerts.

questions.question: Which element has the chemical symbol O?
questions.fact: Oxygen makes up about two-thirds of your body's weight, mostly as part of water.

questions.question: Which type of rock forms when lava cools?
questions.fact: "Igneous" comes from the Latin "ignis", meaning fire. Granite and basalt are both igneous rocks.

questions.question: Which scientist developed the theory of relativity?
questions.fact: Einstein's famous equation is E = mc². He won the Nobel Prize in 1921, but for explaining light, not for relativity.

questions.question: Which scientist described gravity, helped by a famous falling-apple story?
questions.fact: Newton also worked out the laws of motion and showed that white light is a mix of all colours.

questions.question: Who proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.fact: Darwin developed his ideas after a five-year voyage on HMS Beagle, including a visit to the Galápagos Islands.

questions.question: Which scientist won Nobel Prizes in both physics and chemistry?
questions.fact: Marie Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize. Her notebooks are still radioactive today.

questions.question: What is the most common element in the universe?
questions.fact: Hydrogen makes up about three-quarters of the normal matter in the universe. Stars like the Sun are mostly hydrogen.

questions.question: Which part of the Earth is the hottest?
questions.fact: The inner core is about as hot as the surface of the Sun, but it stays solid because of the huge pressure.

questions.question: Which disaster is measured on the Richter scale?
questions.fact: Scientists now usually use the "moment magnitude" scale. Each whole number up means about 32 times more energy.

questions.question: Which layer of the atmosphere protects us from UV rays?
questions.fact: The ozone hole over Antarctica is slowly healing since many countries banned harmful gases called CFCs in 1987.

questions.question: Rust forms when iron reacts with water and…
questions.fact: Stainless steel doesn't rust easily because it contains chromium, which forms a thin protective layer.

questions.question: Which of these is a renewable energy source?
questions.fact: Spain gets a large share of its electricity from wind and sun, among the most in Europe.

questions.question: What was the supercontinent called that broke apart millions of years ago?
questions.fact: "Pangaea" means "all the Earth" in Greek. The continents still drift a few centimetres a year, about as fast as fingernails grow.

questions.question: What does a botanist study?
questions.fact: Botanists have described around 400,000 kinds of plants, and new ones are still being found.

questions.question: Which fruit is famously rich in potassium?
questions.fact: Bananas are slightly radioactive because of their potassium, but completely safe to eat.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for silver?
questions.fact: Ag comes from "argentum", Latin for silver. Argentina was named after silver too.

questions.question: What mainly causes the ocean tides?
questions.fact: Most coasts get two high tides and two low tides roughly every 24 hours and 50 minutes.

questions.question: What is magma called once it reaches the surface?
questions.fact: Fresh lava can be over 1,000 °C. When it cools quickly in water it can form black sand beaches.

questions.question: A cloud that forms at ground level is called…
questions.fact: Fog is just a cloud touching the ground. San Francisco's famous fog even has a nickname: Karl.

questions.question: What is the main gas in natural gas?
questions.fact: Natural gas has no smell. Gas companies add a smelly chemical so that leaks can be noticed quickly.

questions.question: What unit is electrical resistance measured in?
questions.fact: The ohm is named after German physicist Georg Ohm, who studied how electricity flows through wires.

questions.question: Which unit is used to measure power, like a light bulb's?
questions.fact: The watt is named after James Watt, whose improved steam engine helped power the Industrial Revolution.

questions.question: How many legs does an insect have?
questions.fact: Insects have six legs and three body parts: head, thorax and abdomen. There are more kinds of insects than any other animal.

questions.question: What are clouds mostly made of?
questions.fact: A single fluffy cloud can weigh as much as a hundred elephants, because of all the water droplets inside it.

questions.question: Which gas makes fizzy drinks bubbly?
questions.fact: Carbon dioxide dissolves in drinks under pressure. When you open the bottle, it escapes as bubbles.

questions.question: What do we call animals that are active at night?
questions.fact: Owls, bats and hedgehogs are nocturnal. Many have big eyes or great hearing to find food in the dark.

questions.question: What is table salt's chemical name?
questions.fact: Sodium is explosive in water and chlorine is a poisonous gas, but together they make ordinary table salt.

questions.question: What is a material that lets electricity flow easily called?
questions.fact: Copper is one of the best conductors, which is why it's used in most electrical wires.

questions.question: Who discovered penicillin, the first antibiotic?
questions.fact: Fleming discovered penicillin by accident in 1928, when mould grew on a dish of bacteria he had left out.
